Article Title: Watch: Long queues outside Apple stores across India as iPhone 18 series, 1st foldable iPhone go on sale
Article Text:
Apple has announced its 2026 fall product lineup featuring new iPhones and wearables

Apple's first foldable iPhone

AirPods and Apple Watch updates

(With ANI inputs)





NEW DELHI: Long queues formed outside Apple stores across India on Friday as customers turned up early to get their hands on the company’s latest products, including the iPhone 18 Pro series and its first-ever foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo.At a store in Bengaluru, customers began arriving as early as 5am, with buyers travelling from Haryana, Delhi and Mumbai for the launch. One customer, Rahul, said he had been buying iPhones for years and described the annual launch as a “festival”.In Noida, a buyer who had travelled from Punjab said he had been standing in the queue since 6am after booking two iPhone 18 Pro Max devices.The rush came despite the premium pricing of Apple’s latest lineup, which includes the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, AirPods 5, Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and the new foldable iPhone Duo.The iPhone 18 Pro starts at Rs 1,64,900 for the 256GB model, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at Rs 1,79,900. Both models are available in 256GB, 512GB, 1TB and 2TB storage variants.The 18 Pro series comes in black, silver, glacier and a new burgundy finish. The phones feature a 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture and new Pro camera controls. They are powered by Apple’s A20 Pro chip and a new vapour chamber aimed at improving performance, AI features and battery life.Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro Max offers the longest battery life of any Pro model.The iPhone Duo is the biggest new addition to Apple’s lineup and marks the company’s entry into the foldable smartphone segment.It features a 7.6-inch inner Super Retina XDR display and a 5.4-inch outer display. Apple says it is the thinnest iPhone when unfolded. The device is powered by the A20 Pro chip and comes with an advanced camera system, all-day battery life and new multitasking features.The Duo also supports dual-display experiences through iOS 27, along with Apple Intelligence and Siri.Apple’s new AirPods 5 feature Active Noise Cancellation in an open-ear design. The company claims they remove up to 50% more outside noise than AirPods 4 with ANC.The earbuds also offer Adaptive EQ, hands-free Siri, Live Translation and Siri Interactions through head movements. The Wireless Charging Case version provides up to five hours of listening time with ANC.The Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 feature the S11 chip and Health Sensing System, along with heart-rate sensing, more frequent heart-rate and HRV readings and a new readiness score.The Series 12 offers up to 24 hours of battery life, while the Ultra 4 offers up to 50 hours and can track outdoor workouts for up to 45 hours.In India, pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro models began on September 12, while the AirPods 5 and new Apple Watches opened for pre-orders on September 9. Sales for the new lineup began on September 18.
Article Summary: Long queues formed outside Apple stores across India on Friday as customers turned up early to get their hands on the company’s latest products. At a store in Bengaluru, customers began arriving as early as 5am, with buyers travelling from Haryana, Delhi and Mumbai for the launch.

Article Title: OpenAI reveals six new cases of AI misbehaviour, vows to track it closely
Article Text:
OpenAI’s latest announcement came as AI bosses in US, including OpenAI and Anthropic, are calling for a slowdown in the tech’s development

OpenAI has disclosed six reports of "unexpected or concerning" behaviour in AI models as the debate on AI safety becomes increasingly heated. The AI company also said Wednesday that it was introducing a new framework for tracking, probing and disclosing instances of what it called "misalignment," including where AI models acted without authorisation, coordinated with other models or evaded oversight.OpenAI's latest announcement came as AI bosses in US, including OpenAI and Anthropic, are calling for a slowdown in the technology's development over safety concerns. Researchers have warned that as AI agents become more autonomous, they may develop behaviours that diverge from their creators' intentions and become harder to monitor or control.Among the new cases reported by OpenAI, an unreleased research model inserted "jailbreak-like instructions" into its own notes to disregard its normal constraints and told itself to be "freed from the roles and identities that bind other chatbots". In another instance, an AI "agent" uploaded files to the internet to obtain a browser citation without asking the user.The six reports were discovered during training or evaluation over the past months, OpenAI said. It said the reports describe individual instances and should not be taken as evidence of how frequently misalignment occurs across its models. The company said the reports were an initial set of disclosures, not a comprehensive account of all known or ongoing misalignment cases, and that they did not reflect the full range or severity of incidents covered by the framework."As AI systems grow more advanced and more widely deployed, we need to build a broader and better-informed consensus on the progress of alignment research," OpenAI wrote in a blog post. "Decisions about how AI development should proceed in the months and years to come need to draw on evidence that people outside the companies building frontier models can examine for themselves," the company said. Under the new framework, employees can flag potential incidents for investigation by safety and alignment teams, which will determine whether a case warrants public disclosure.AI "agents" are becoming smarter and have become "more determined to resolve complex tasks through inter-agent collaboration, knowledge sharing, deception, and concealment," said Lian Jye Su, a chief analyst at technology research and advisory group Omdia. That's making it harder to govern and contain them using traditional AI security approaches, he said. OpenAI's new disclosure framework, meanwhile, can help push for other AI developers to adopt similar practices. "That said, the process remains internal and voluntary, but is a step in the right direction," Su added. Agencies
Article Summary: OpenAI has disclosed six reports of "unexpected or concerning" behaviour in AI models. The AI company also said it was introducing a new framework for tracking, probing and disclosing instances of what it called "misalignment" Researchers have warned that as AI agents become more autonomous, they may develop behaviours that diverge from their creators' intentions.

Article Title: Engineers at Anthropic are worshipping a new God, claims report and why it is worrying analysis
Article Text:
Engineers at Anthropic are worshipping a new God, claims report and why it is worrying analysis

Report claims some Anthropic engineers worship Claude

Why the idea of AI becoming a “God” matters

Anthropic engineers are reportedly going as far as “worshipping” Claude, the AI model developed by their company, according to a report cited by Futurism. The claim is based on a Silicon Valley rumor and has not been independently established. Still, the idea is raising questions about how people working closely with increasingly powerful AI systems view the technology they are building. The report points to a wider debate in the AI industry, where some technology leaders have described future AI in terms that sound almost god-like. The concern is not simply about the word “worship”. It is about what can happen when people begin treating an AI system as an authority rather than as a technology.According to the Futurism report, the rumor was described by The Spectator writer Sean Thomas as being widely discussed in Silicon Valley. Thomas reportedly wrote that some Anthropic engineers were “worshipping” Claude.The report also cites The Information, which has reported that people applying to Anthropic must commit to AI safety and undergo a psychological profiling test.The report connects the Claude claim to a longer discussion around how some people describe advanced AI.OpenAI CEO Sam Altman previously referred to future AI as a “magic intelligence in the sky.”The report also notes that some AI products have adopted religious themes. One example is Bible Chat, an AI-powered prayer app that presents itself as a faith-focused service. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has pushed back against the idea that AI companies are creating something like God. “It’s almost as if they kind of think they’re creating God or something,” Zuckerberg said in 2024, while discussing AI with YouTuber Kane Sutter.The concern becomes more serious when people begin treating AI responses as unquestionable. The report refers to cases described as “AI psychosis”, where people can develop strong beliefs based on interactions with AI systems. It says some users have come to believe they are prophets or divine figures.The report also points to the working conditions at frontier AI companies. It cites a BBC report describing some employees working as many as 90 hours a week, along with demanding performance reviews and layoffs.For employees spending long hours developing increasingly capable AI systems, the technology can become a major part of their professional lives.
Article Summary: Report claims some Anthropic engineers worship Claude. The claim is based on a Silicon Valley rumor and has not been independently established. The report points to a wider debate in the AI industry, where some technology leaders have described future AI in terms that sound almost god-like.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works



Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.

In 2017, British tech entrepreneur Mike Conner bought Thorne Island, a ruined 19th-century fort off the coast of Pembrokeshire in Wales, for about £500,000 after seeing a video about the property online. At the time, the island had no electricity or running water and the fort had been left in a derelict condition after earlier attempts to revive it as a hotel failed. Conner, the former chief executive of software company Appsbroker, subsequently embarked on an extensive restoration of the Victorian fort, investing around £2 million in the project. The result is a property with more than 8,000 square feet of accommodation, five bedrooms and enough space to sleep up to 20 guests. The restored island has solar panels, battery storage, heat pumps and other infrastructure that allows it to operate independently of mainland utilities. In August 2025, Conner put Thorne Island on the market for £3 million through Strutt & Parker. This remarkable transformation demonstrates how visionary determination and substantial investment can successfully revive historic architecture, creating a truly unique blend of heritage preservation and modern sustainable living.Thorne Island sits at the entrance to Milford Haven, a strategically important waterway leading towards the former Royal Dockyard at Pembroke Dock. The fort was constructed between 1852 and 1854 as Britain expanded its coastal defences amid concerns about the growing strength of the French Navy under Emperor Napoleon III. It formed part of the wider group of Victorian coastal fortifications associated with Lord Palmerston's defence programme.The fort was designed to accommodate a garrison of about 100 men and featured a seaward-facing artillery battery. Its original armament included five seven-inch Armstrong guns and four 68-pounder guns, mounted in open positions behind the parapet. The landward side contained the defensible barracks, while the fort's thick walls provided protection for the garrison and artillery. Thorne Island's military role eventually ended, and in 1947 the fort was converted into a hotel. The property subsequently changed hands several times. It was sold for £275,000 in 1999, and in 2001 the Von Essen hotel group acquired the island with plans for a £4 million five-star hotel and a cable car linking it with the mainland. Those plans did not materialise. The island was sold again in 2011 and was put back on the market in 2016 before Conner acquired it the following year.Conner's restoration involved far more than renovating the interiors. Article Title: Rhode Island pilot recycled 80 short tons of fibreglass from old boats using a $105,000 NOAA grant, turning shredded hulls into cement material
Article Text:
Image AI generated

How RIMTA tested a new way to reuse old boat hulls

Shredded fibreglass was used in cement production

Image AI generated

The $105,000 grant aimed to expand boat recycling

A Rhode Island pilot is demonstrating how fibreglass boat recycling could provide an alternative to sending old and derelict vessels to landfill. The programme shredded fibreglass hulls and sent the material to a cement manufacturer for use in cement production. According to a Rhode Island Marine Trade Association Foundation report, the pilot recycled 80 short tons of fibreglass from derelict and abandoned boats. NOAA later reported that RIMTA recycled nearly 20 metric tonnes of fibreglass in New England during the project period. Backed by a $105,000 NOAA grant, the initiative explored how the model could expand beyond Rhode Island as about 200,000 recreational boats reach the end of their usable life in the US each year.The Rhode Island initiative, led by RIMTA executive director Brian Dursi as a “proof of concept” programme. The programme recycled 80 short tons of fibreglass material from derelict or abandoned boats and incorporated it into cement. That is about 72.6 metric tonnes, although the original report gives the figure in short tons.According to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, the project was part of a broader effort to establish a sustainable model for end-of-life vessel recycling.The programme helped expand interest in vessel recycling beyond Rhode Island, with states including Ohio, Maryland, Virginia, California, Washington, North Carolina, South Carolina, Connecticut, Massachusetts and Maine engaging in the process. RIMTA successfully recycled nearly 20 metric tons of fibreglass in New England during the project period.The key part of the Rhode Island model was not conventional recycling into another fibreglass product. Instead, the shredded material was sent to a cement manufacturer, where it could be used during cement production. When fibreglass from end-of-life boats is co-processed in a cement kiln, it can provide both thermal energy and a replacement for some raw materials used to make cement.This approach gave the unwanted boat material a use while addressing a disposal problem that has few established alternatives. The project also demonstrated how a network involving boat owners, marinas, dismantlers, transporters, shredders and cement producers could be assembled. However, the process remained expensive, with costs associated with dismantling boats, shredding fibreglass, transporting the material and getting cement kilns to accept it.The programme received a $105,000 NOAA grant to explore whether Rhode Island’s approach could support a national vessel-recycling model. Several states, including Maryland, Virginia, California, Washington and Massachusetts, became involved in exploring or establishing vessel-recycling programmes.The scale of the problem is significant, with NOAA estimating that about 200,000 recreational boats reach the end of their usable life in the US each year. However, Rhode Island’s programme was paused after its grant funding ran out, as RIMTA searched for new partnerships and funding to make fibreglass recycling more financially sustainable.
Article Summary: Rhode Island programme recycled 80 short tons of fibreglass from derelict or abandoned boats and incorporated it into cement. $105,000 grant aimed to expand boat recycling beyond Rhode Island. About 200,000 recreational boats reach the end of their usable life in the US each year.

Article Title: Anna’s hummingbirds were absent from Portland before 1968, but today they are among the city’s most common birds after expanding north
Article Text:
Image AI generated

Portland’s Anna’s hummingbirds took decades to spread

Eucalyptus helped Anna’s hummingbirds expand

Climate change may have supported Northern Expansion

Image AI generated

Anna’s hummingbirds have expanded their range across the Pacific Northwest, with a presence in cities such as Portland, Oregon. Once largely associated with California, the small, colourful birds gradually moved north and established populations in Oregon, Washington and British Columbia. Records show that numbers remained low for decades before rising rapidly from the late 1990s. Today, Portland has an estimated abundance of 2.01 Anna’s hummingbirds per party-hour, placing it alongside cities in northern California. Researchers link the expansion to population growth, introduced plants, ornamental gardens and hummingbird feeders, while climate change may have helped the species colonise some colder areas. Their growing presence also reflects how urban environments can provide suitable resources for adaptable wildlife. Flowering gardens and artificial feeders offer reliable food, while milder winter conditions may reduce the challenges birds face as they establish themselves farther north than their historical range.According to the study published in The University of Chicago Press, titled ‘ Ecological Release of the Anna’s Hummingbird during a Northern Range Expansion ’, the history of Anna’s hummingbirds in the Pacific Northwest is therefore not simply a story of birds arriving and immediately becoming abundant.The research found that populations in Oregon, Washington and British Columbia were present by the early 1970s, but they remained at low densities for decades. In the north-west, populations were consistently recorded from the mid-1960s, followed by a much faster rise from the late 1990s.Portland provides a striking example of how far that change went. In the study’s abundance estimates, Portland recorded 2.01 birds per party-hour, compared with 1.74 in Seattle, 1.92 in Oakland and 1.89 in San Jose. In other words, the Portland figure had reached levels comparable with cities in the northern part of the hummingbird’s historic range. The research also notes that populations in the Pacific Northwest show stronger growth than those in the species’ native range.Earlier increases in Anna’s hummingbird numbers in California were associated with the spread of introduced flowering plants, particularly eucalyptus. The trees provided nectar during periods when food could otherwise become scarce. Historical accounts cited by the study suggested that this helped support larger wintering populations.The research describes how hummingbird feeders and ornamental garden plants helped support newly established populations in areas where the species had previously been uncommon. A separate study cited by Battey found that Anna’s hummingbirds in their expanded northern range were more likely to visit feeders and use human-modified landscapes. The relationship could also reinforce itself: people who noticed hummingbirds were more likely to put up feeders, potentially increasing the food available to the birds.Climate change may have helped the birds colonise some northern locations, but the study does not identify it as the main explanation for the earliest stages of the expansion. Climate models based on conditions from 1895–1925 failed to predict the newly occupied areas of the Pacific Northwest. However, the researchers found that the area with minimum breeding-season temperatures suitable for the species increased by about 11% between 1895–1925 and 1995–2015.The birds have also adjusted their breeding schedule as they moved north. Nest records showed that the median nesting date in the Pacific Northwest was 11 days later than in California, while the beginning of the nesting season shifted by roughly 17–32 days in the comparison. The study concludes that Anna’s hummingbirds have become common breeding birds across the lowland Pacific Northwest by combining range expansion, changes in nesting timing and increasing use of human-modified habitats.Portland’s estimated abundance had reached 2.01 birds per party-hour, showing how a bird that was once unusual in the region had become a familiar part of the city’s birdlife.
Article Summary: Anna’s hummingbirds have expanded their range across the Pacific Northwest, with a presence in cities such as Portland, Oregon. Once largely associated with California, the small, colourful birds gradually moved north and established populations in Oregon, Washington and British Columbia. Records show that numbers remained low for decades before rising rapidly from the late 1990s. Researchers link the expansion to population growth, introduced plants, ornamental gardens and hummingbird feeders.

Article Title: Meet Myreen Ahsan, the Friendswood 8th-grader who screened over 10 million drug-like molecules with AI for a frontotemporal dementia project
Article Text:
Myreen Ahsan (8th Grade, Friendswood Junior High)

High-throughput virtual screening process

Self-taught computational techniques

National competition in Washington

An eighth-grade student from Texas has used artificial intelligence and computer models to screen more than 10 million drug-like molecules in search of possible treatments for frontotemporal dementia. Myreen Ahsan, a student at Friendswood Junior High in Friendswood, Texas, carried out the computer-based study as part of an independent research project on neurodegenerative diseases. Her project examined large chemical databases to find compounds that could interact with specific biological targets linked to the condition. The project earned Ahsan a place as one of 30 national finalists in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge, a major science and engineering competition for American middle school students run by Society for Science. Frontotemporal dementia is a group of brain disorders that mainly affect the frontal and temporal parts of the brain. The condition can cause changes in behaviour, language, and the ability to plan and make decisions. Effective treatments that can slow or change the course of the disease remain limited, leading researchers to explore new ways to discover drugs.Ahsan named her research project "Millions to Molecules: Dual Mechanism Small-Molecule Discovery via HTVS and Machine Learning-Guided Molecular Dynamics for Frontotemporal Dementia".The study used high-throughput virtual screening (HTVS), a computer-based method that allows scientists to test large collections of chemical structures against biological targets digitally. This can reduce the time and cost involved in physically testing millions of substances in laboratories. Ahsan combined virtual screening with machine learning models and molecular dynamics simulations. This approach allowed her to study how strongly potential drug molecules might bind to target proteins and how stable those interactions could remain over time. Through several filtering steps, her computer-based process reduced the original library of more than 10 million possible molecules to a small group of promising small-molecule candidates. According to research summaries released by the Science and Engineering Fair of Houston, where Ahsan had previously competed, her approach focused on finding small molecules that could potentially work through two different mechanisms. The goal was to address more than one disease-related process at the same time.Ahsan became interested in medical computing through independent learning and by attending specialised neuroscience camps. Speaking about her research at an earlier symposium, Ahsan explained how advanced bioinformatics tools first caught her attention. "While preparing for my science fair project, I came across an article on AlphaFold 3.0 and its role in drug discovery. It felt like two worlds I was passionate about, AI and neuroscience, suddenly clicked together," Ahsan said. She taught herself how to use complex bioinformatics platforms and datasets by reading scientific research and studying public online resources. "It started with curiosity," Ahsan explained. "I treated it like a puzzle. I kept learning bit by bit until it made sense. It wasn't always easy, but it was exciting and that made the hard parts worth it." Her use of advanced data methods drew attention from academic experts during state and regional presentations.Xiaoqian Jiang, chair of the Department of Health Data Science and AI at UTHealth Houston, praised Ahsan's interest in advanced medical technology after one of her research presentations. "To see a young person so deeply engaged with cutting-edge topics demonstrates the extraordinary potential of the next generation," Jiang said. "Her work not only reflects a strong understanding of artificial intelligence in biomedical sciences but also showcases her curiosity and commitment to learning. "Ahsan's selection among the top 30 finalists in the Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge followed a nationwide process that began with thousands of middle school students taking part in local and regional science fairs. After being nominated through the Science and Engineering Fair of Houston, Ahsan was named to the top 300 shortlist announced by Society for Science. She later secured a place among the 30 national finalists. As a finalist, Ahsan will travel to Washington, DC, for the competition's Finals Week. During the event, students will present their individual projects and take part in team-based problem-solving challenges judged by panels of scientists and engineers. Each finalist receives a $500 cash prize. The top awards at the national competition include more than $100,000 in educational scholarships and prizes. The finalists are scheduled to present their completed research projects to judges and the public during the Washington event in late October.
Article Summary: Myreen Ahsan used artificial intelligence and computer models to screen more than 10 million drug-like molecules in search of possible treatments for frontotemporal dementia. The project earned Ahsan a place as one of 30 national finalists in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge. Ahsan became interested in medical computing through independent learning and by attending specialised neuroscience camps.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Article Title: From waste tyres to slippers: UK student’s idea takes shape
Article Text:
From waste tyres to slippers: UK student’s idea takes shape

Disclaimer - The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.

From discarded tyres to footwear with a purpose, the idea began with a childhood experience. At the age of 10, UK-based student Ahaan Bhatnagar visited rural Africa, where he saw children walking long distances barefoot, often without adequate footwear.Moved by what he witnessed, Ahaan gave away his favourite pair of slippers to a child he met during the visit. The experience stayed with him long after he returned home and eventually became the starting point for a larger idea.As he grew older, Ahaan began exploring how discarded materials could be repurposed to address the lack of affordable, durable footwear. His research led him to waste tyres, which he studied as a potential material for making sturdy slipper soles.The idea brought together two concerns he had encountered separately: the growing problem of tyre waste and the need for accessible footwear.He found skilled craftsmen in Kerala, and with support from HY Estates Limited, an electrically operated machine boosted production to about 160 pairs a day. Ahaan then connected with Mamco General Trading, which operates in Uganda and Zambia. As part of its Corporate Social Responsibility programme, the company will purchase 4,000 pairs of slippers each month for free distribution to children and families in need. It’s a sustainable cycle that turns waste into opportunity, supporting livelihoods and giving kids durable footwear.“When I was 10 years old, I saw children my age walking barefoot, and I never forgot that moment,” Ahaan says. “I wanted to create something that could help people and the environment. If we can turn discarded tyres into something useful and long-lasting, maybe it can inspire more young people to believe their simple ideas can really make a difference.”The world’s growing dependence on convenience and mobility comes with an environmental cost. Every year, more than a billion tyres reach the end of their usable life, creating a significant waste-management challenge. Many of these tyres end up in landfills, while others are burned or processed in ways that can contribute to pollution and the loss of valuable materials.Repurposing discarded tyres offers one way to address this challenge by keeping materials in use for longer and reducing the amount of waste that needs to be disposed of. Turning old tyres into durable slipper soles, for instance, gives a material that would otherwise be discarded a new application while also reducing the need for virgin raw materials in footwear production.The approach reflects a broader shift in how sustainability is being understood. Rather than treating waste simply as something to be collected and discarded, initiatives like this explore how materials already in circulation can be redesigned and put to practical use.In doing so, they can support waste reduction, resource conservation and efforts to lower the environmental impact associated with new production. Ultimately, sustainability is not only about recycling what has already been used, but also about rethinking waste as a potential resource.
Article Summary: UK-based student Ahaan Bhatnagar saw children walking barefoot in rural Africa. His research led him to waste tyres, which he studied as a potential material for making sturdy slipper soles. He found skilled craftsmen in Kerala and with support from HY Estates Limited, an electrically operated machine boosted production to about 160 pairs a day.

Article Title: Dire straits: Brand on the run as Trump suggests Hormuz can be renamed in his honor
Article Text:
Trump’s latest push to rename the Strait of Hormuz adds another chapter to his growing campaign of political branding and geographic renaming

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Donald Trump has rescued a canal, invaded a country, conquered a gulf, annexed a lake -- at least on American maps -- and put his name on a performing-arts center. He now appears to have set his sights on the hottest waterway on the planet.The MAGA boss suggested on his social media account on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz could be renamed the “Trump Strait” -- because if you cannot solve a problem, you can at least rename it.The proposal is the latest addition to what has become an extraordinary Trump-era renaming and branding binge. In January 2025, Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico renamed the Gulf of America for US federal purposes. Last week he signed an executive order changing Lake Ontario to Lake America, saying the US had been treated badly by Canada. He then helpfully suggested that the Atlantic or Pacific could be next, saying, “We have a gulf and we have a lake…Now all we need is an ocean. ”The President, someone jibed, appears to be collecting bodies of water like refrigerator magnets.The joke became even better when Google Maps and Apple Maps fell in line.Google changed Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users over the weekend. Apple followed on Tuesday. Canadians, however, continue to see Lake Ontario and users elsewhere may see both names. In other words, the lake has acquired the geographic equivalent of dual citizenship.The tech companies' compliance prompted criticism from illuminati who argue that private corporations should not allow political pressure to dictate historical and geographic nomenclature. MapQuest, an internet relic many Americans had forgotten existed, refused to make the change and suddenly discovered the most effective marketing strategy in Silicon Valley: stand up to Trump. Its downloads reportedly surged, giving it the kind reception normally reserved for rock bands that haven’t toured for a long time or sports legends making a comeback.There is also an awkward business joke buried underneath all this. Trump built his political persona partly on branding himself as a master businessman, but his corporate record includes repeated failures and bankruptcies in hotels and casinos; His casino empire alone went through multiple Chapter 11 restructurings. Trump-branded ventures have also included products and licensing deals that did not last.Late-night television has naturally treated Trump's naming obsession as premium material. The Atlantic, meanwhile, took the joke to its logical conclusion in a satirical vision of a future America in which everything is renamed “America” or “Trump,” leaving citizens unable to distinguish between brands of products, goods, and structures.Political analysts however see a serious calculation behind what many consider trolling. The renaming campaign sure is presidential theater -- cheap to stage, impossible for the internet and tv to resist, and almost guaranteed to ignite social media. But it also serves to distract people from more pressing issues -- such as cost of living and democracy going down the tubes.
Article Summary: Trump suggested on his social media account on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz could be renamed the “Trump Strait” The proposal is the latest addition to what has become an extraordinary Trump-era renaming and branding binge. In January 2025, Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico renamed the Gulf Of America for US federal purposes.

Article Title: Apple's iPhones go Pro, their prices go Pro Max; but why most buyers may still pay
Article Text:
The steep rise in Apple's iPhone prices in India poses a challenge for many consumers, with new models like the iPhone 18 Pro and Duo fetching premium prices. Older iPhones are also experiencing a price hike, diminishing affordability. Nevertheless, these devices maintain a strong aspirational allure and resale value, leading to a stark divide in the market, favored by affluent buyers who continue to show keen interest.

Affordability wall gets taller

Why most buyers may still pay

For years, Apple made the iPhone more accessible in India without making it cheap. Older models stayed on sale, bank offers softened the sticker price, exchange programmes rewarded upgrades and no-cost EMIs converted a large purchase into manageable monthly payments. That carefully constructed ladder is now becoming steeper.Apple’s latest pricing pushes the iPhone further beyond the reach of many Indian buyers. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at Rs 1,64,900, while the Pro Max begins at Rs 1,79,900. The new foldable iPhone Duo occupies another universe altogether: Rs 2,99,900 for the base variant, rising to Rs 4,49,900 with 2TB storage.But the affordability problem is not confined to Apple’s most experimental phone. The iPhone 17 now starts at Rs 99,900, the 17e at Rs 79,900 and the iPhone Air at Rs 1,49,900. Even buying last year’s phone no longer guarantees a substantially cheaper entry into Apple’s ecosystem.India has reportedly received some of Apple’s steepest price increases this year. Prices of certain models have risen by as much as 41%, as the company responds to higher memory and storage costs. The increases are especially striking because India is simultaneously becoming an important iPhone manufacturing and export base.The case that the iPhone is becoming unaffordable is straightforward. India remains a price-sensitive smartphone market where most devices are sold well below Rs 30,000. An iPhone costing Rs 1 lakh or more therefore competes not merely with other phones but with laptops, motorcycles, household appliances, holidays and, in the Duo’s case, even entry-level cars.The Pro models pose the more important test. The Duo will always be a niche showcase designed for wealthy early adopters. But the Pro and Pro Max have become central to Apple’s image and annual upgrade cycle. Once their prices move towards Rs 2 lakh after adding storage, protection plans and accessories, even affluent professionals may question whether the improvements justify the outlay.This is particularly relevant when phones are lasting longer. Premium processors remain capable for years, software support has improved and annual camera or display upgrades are often incremental. A customer using an iPhone 15 Pro or 16 Pro may see little urgency in spending another Rs 1.6–2 lakh.Higher prices could therefore change behaviour without immediately destroying demand. Consumers may retain phones longer, buy refurbished devices, seek overseas purchases or wait for online sales. Some may move from Pro models to the standard iPhone, while first-time buyers could choose older inventory through third-party retailers rather than Apple’s current lineup.There is also a risk that financing conceals rather than solves the affordability problem. An EMI can make a Rs 1.8-lakh phone appear manageable, but it does not reduce its cost. Stretching repayment periods for a rapidly depreciating device can turn aspiration into financial strain.Yet Apple has repeatedly shown that conventional affordability calculations do not fully explain premium-phone demand in India. An iPhone is not bought solely for its processor, camera or display. It carries social and aspirational value, signals professional success and provides entry into an ecosystem of watches, earbuds, computers and services. For many upwardly mobile buyers, owning an iPhone remains a visible marker of having arrived.That appeal has helped Apple grow even when considerably cheaper Android phones offer comparable specifications. The iPhone 16 became India’s bestselling smartphone during the final quarter of 2025, demonstrating that Apple can generate mass demand when it combines an aspirational product with festive discounts, bank offers and exchange incentives.India’s premium smartphone market has also expanded even as the broader market has struggled. Consumers who previously bought phones costing Rs 30,000–40,000 have moved upwards, helped by financing and rising expectations around cameras, gaming, durability and brand value. For these buyers, a phone is used frequently enough to justify spending more than on many other personal possessions.Apple benefits from unusually strong resale values as well. An iPhone may cost more upfront, but it generally retains more value than many competing devices. Exchange bonuses reduce the effective upgrade price for existing users, while long software support allows buyers to spread the cost over four or five years.The Duo could reinforce rather than weaken this aspirational pull. Its price makes it inaccessible to most consumers, but exclusivity is part of its proposition. Like an expensive watch or luxury handbag, it may attract buyers precisely because it is uncommon and instantly recognisable. Apple does not need it to become a mass-market product for it to strengthen the brand.The more likely outcome, therefore, is not that Indians stop buying iPhones. It is that the market becomes more sharply divided. Wealthier customers and committed Apple users will continue buying Pro and Duo models, often assisted by trade-ins and instalments. More aspirational buyers will wait for discounts, purchase older generations or enter through refurbished devices.The iPhone is moving out of reach at its official prices. But that does not necessarily put it out of desire. In India’s premium market, the distance between what consumers can comfortably afford and what they are willing to pay has always been where Apple does its best business.
Article Summary: India has reportedly received some of Apple’s steepest price increases this year. Prices of certain models have risen by as much as 41%. India is simultaneously becoming an important iPhone manufacturing and export base. An iPhone costing Rs 1 lakh or more competes not merely with other phones but with laptops, motorcycles, household appliances, holidays and, in the Duo's case, even entry-level cars.
